source_notice: Egypt / EGP Full Evidence Rebuild (GO → from-scratch over legacy inventory). Legacy managed-float, symmetric USD10k entry/exit declaration, resident general-authorisation, non-resident 'more freely', and bank-only settlement claims are retired. Primary Law 194 evidence is closed against the Official Gazette Arabic text of Law No. 194 of 2020 (الجريدة الرسمية — العدد 37 مكرر (و) — 15 سبتمبر سنة 2020), hosted as the NIB.gov.eg government library PDF and indexed on the CBE Banking Laws page; Arts 211–215 pinned at Official Gazette / PDF pages 106–107 (مادة ٢١١–٢١٥). Andersen English translation removed from governed source_authorities/source_map (not CBE/legislature/Official Gazette; not primary). Art. 211: Board FX-market rules; EGP rate by supply/demand (بتفاعل قوى العرض والطلب). Art. 212: every natural/legal person may retain FX and conduct FX operations including inward/outward transfers through banks or other licensed entities under Board rules; domestic transactions in EGP unless treaty/other law/Board case. Art. 213 asymmetric cash: inbound foreign currency free with disclosure when amount exceeds (جاوز) USD 10,000 equivalent — strictly >; no general inbound quantitative ceiling; outbound ordinary carriage not exceeding (ألا يزيد على) USD 10,000 equivalent — <=; previously disclosed inbound remainder may be carried at departure even if above USD 10,000; EGP banknotes within Board-set limit; postal cash prohibited. Board Decision No. 2200 of 2020 numeric status is closed: Official Gazette / الوقائع المصرية — العدد 220 (تابع) — 30 سبتمبر سنة 2020 Art. 1 sets physical EGP carriage at five thousand Egyptian pounds for persons entering or leaving Egypt; effective day after publication; governed URL pin is the CBE Other Laws official index (Decision 2200/2020 still listed; CBE-hosted Decision PDF not publicly downloadable at execution); no later replacing Board instrument located on the reviewed CBE corpus through execution date. Art. 214 banks' FX powers; Art. 215 banks/exchange companies/licensed FX entities report to CBE; CBE On-Site Supervision page confirms multi-channel licensed FX market. Monetary regime: Special MPC 6 March 2024 — exchange rate determined by market forces while transitioning to flexible inflation targeting; Q2 2026 Monetary Policy Report and live Market Exchange Rate / CBE Exchange Rates pages (updated through early Sept 2026) treat the market rate as operative — not 'managed floating'. BNI remains a Pinpoint residual: Art. 213 itself is foreign-currency cash (نقد أجنبي), not bearer negotiable instruments; AML Law 80/2002 Art. 12 + executive regulations may create a separate/parallel customs declaration layer including BNI — current consolidated numeric architecture vs Art. 213 left for Pinpoint (do not fold BNI into Art. 213). 2024–2026 Foreign Currency Activities circular sweep: no post–6 March 2024 circular located that re-imposes a general resident FX-holding authorisation or resurrects shortage-era bank-only settlement as eligibility law; operational reporting (including exchange-company AML systems) is distinguished from legal eligibility. Passage Check posture remains Publication-stage / unpublished; evaluated candidate on existing taxonomy leans floating_regulated_market but is deferred/unlocked. Egypt remains unpublished rehabilitation inventory outside candidate intake.
country_overview: Egypt's currency is the Egyptian pound (EGP). Under Law No. 194 of 2020 Art. 211, the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) Board issues the rules governing the foreign-exchange market, and the EGP exchange rate against foreign currencies is determined by the interaction of supply and demand in that market — a market-determined exchange-rate framework kept analytically separate from FX-channel regulation. The CBE Special MPC of 6 March 2024 stated that the exchange rate is allowed to be determined by market forces while the CBE continues transitioning toward a flexible inflation-targeting regime; current 2026 CBE Monetary Policy Report and live market/CBE exchange-rate pages treat the market-determined rate as operative. Cross-border FX operations are regulated and must be conducted through banks or other entities licensed under Law 194, subject to Board rules (Art. 212) — not an unregulated free-for-all and not a claim of unrestricted convertibility of every source of funds. Physical foreign-currency carriage is asymmetric under Art. 213 (inbound disclosure trigger vs outbound ordinary ceiling), and physical EGP banknote carriage is a separate Board-set limit under Art. 213 / Board Decision No. 2200 of 2020 (five thousand EGP for persons entering or leaving Egypt). Absence of a located restriction is not evidence that none exists.

summary.traveler: Under Law 194/2020 Art. 213, foreign currency may be brought into Egypt by all arrivals with no general quantitative import ceiling; amounts exceeding USD 10,000 (or equivalent) must be disclosed on the prescribed form (Arabic جاوز — strictly >; exactly USD 10,000 is outside the inbound disclosure trigger). On departure, foreign currency may ordinarily be taken out provided it does not exceed USD 10,000 (or equivalent) (ألا يزيد على — <=); travellers may also carry the remainder of foreign currency previously disclosed on arrival even where that remainder exceeds USD 10,000. Physical Egyptian-pound banknotes may be carried only within the Board-set limit under Art. 213 / Board Decision No. 2200 of 2020: five thousand EGP for persons entering or leaving Egypt (Official Gazette / الوقائع المصرية Issue 220 Supplement, 30 Sept 2020, Art. 1). These regimes are not a single symmetric 'USD 10,000 declaration at entry and exit'.
summary.business: Law 194/2020 Art. 212 permits natural and legal persons to conduct FX operations, including inward and outward transfers, through banks or other licensed entities under Board rules and procedures. Domestic transactions inside Egypt are in EGP unless an international agreement, another law, or a Board-authorised case provides otherwise. Arts 214–215 and CBE supervision establish a licensed multi-channel FX market (banks, exchange companies and other licensed FX entities), not a bank-only monopoly. This is not a claim that every cross-border payment is unrestricted.

rules.bring_foreign_currency_in: Law 194/2020 Art. 213 provides that bringing foreign currency into Egypt is guaranteed for all arrivals. There is no general quantitative inbound import ceiling in Art. 213. Disclosure on the prescribed form is required when the amount exceeds USD 10,000 or its equivalent in other foreign currencies (Arabic: إذا جاوز عشرة آلاف دولار — strictly 'exceeds' / 'جاوز', not '>=' / 'USD 10,000 or more'). Exactly USD 10,000 is outside the inbound disclosure trigger. This is a declaration/disclosure trigger, not an import ceiling. Art. 213's inbound limb addresses foreign currency (نقد أجنبي); bearer negotiable instruments are not silently folded into this Art. 213 threshold.
rules.take_foreign_currency_out: Outbound foreign-currency cash under Law 194/2020 Art. 213 is not symmetric with inbound. Ordinary departure rule: foreign currency may be taken out provided it does not exceed USD 10,000 or equivalent (Arabic: بشرط ألا يزيد على عشرة آلاف دولار — ordinary physical-carriage ceiling, operator <=). Separate exception: at departure, travellers may carry what remains of amounts previously disclosed upon arrival even where that remainder exceeds USD 10,000. Do not publish a symmetric 'USD 10,000 declaration at entry and exit'. Postal conveyance of Egyptian or foreign cash by letters/parcels is prohibited under Art. 213. Physical EGP banknotes are a separate Board-limit regime (Decision 2200/2020).
rules.cash_declaration_threshold: Two distinct Art. 213 foreign-currency architectures plus a separate EGP banknote limit. (1) Inbound foreign currency: mandatory disclosure when value exceeds USD 10,000 equivalent (جاوز / strictly >); no general inbound ceiling. (2) Outbound foreign currency: ordinary carriage not exceeding USD 10,000 equivalent (<=), plus documented previously-disclosed inbound remainder exception above that amount. (3) Physical EGP banknotes: Board Decision No. 2200 of 2020 Art. 1 — carriage permitted within five thousand Egyptian pounds for persons entering or leaving Egypt (Official Gazette / الوقائع المصرية Issue 220 Supplement, 30 Sept 2020; effective day after publication; CBE Other Laws still lists Decision 2200/2020; no later replacing Board instrument located on the reviewed CBE corpus). Do not collapse these into one symmetric USD 10,000 entry/exit declaration figure, and do not treat the EGP banknote limit as a foreign-currency declaration threshold. BNI remains unresolved relative to Art. 213 and is not mapped here.
rules.resident_holding_rules: Law 194/2020 Art. 212 establishes that every natural or legal person may retain, own or possess foreign currency accruing to, owned by or held by that person, and may conduct foreign-exchange operations including inward and outward transfers, through banks or other entities licensed under the Law, according to rules and procedures set by the CBE Board. This retires the legacy claim that Egyptian residents generally require specific authorisation for unrestricted FX holding. Art. 212 is an eligibility / channel architecture, not a guaranteed entitlement to every bank product or account type, and not permission to deal outside licensed channels. Domestic transactions inside Egypt must be in EGP unless an international agreement, another law, or a Board-authorised case provides otherwise — a domestic settlement rule kept separate from international transfer rights.
rules.non_resident_rules: Art. 212 is framed for every natural or legal person and does not, on its face, create a more-liberal non-resident transfer baseline. Legacy wording that non-residents 'transfer funds more freely' is retired absent a current primary source establishing a real residency divergence. Non-resident and resident treatment therefore start from the same Art. 212 licensed-channel baseline. Any specific non-resident account-product categories found in current CBE circulars/directories remain transaction-specific and are not asserted as a general freer convertibility right in this Evidence Rebuild.
rules.business_invoicing_settlement: Cross-border FX settlement follows Art. 212: operations including inward/outward transfers through banks or other licensed entities under Board rules — not bank-only. Art. 214 authorises banks to conduct FX operations (deposits, dealing, inward/outward transfers, deployment/cover); banks may import/export foreign currencies with CBE approval. Art. 215 requires banks, exchange companies and other licensed FX entities to report FX operations to the CBE, which supervises implementation. Domestic Egyptian transactions default to EGP under Art. 212 unless a legal exception applies. A 2024–2026 Foreign Currency Activities / related circular currentness sweep through execution date did not locate a post–6 March 2024 instrument re-imposing shortage-era general FX-access denial or a universal bank-only eligibility rule; operational reporting requirements are distinguished from legal eligibility. Absence of a located transaction-specific restriction is not evidence that none exists.
rules.exchange_controls: Egypt's Law 194/2020 architecture is not usefully summarised as legacy 'managed float with resident capital controls / largely liberalised current account'. The statute establishes: (i) market-determined EGP rate by supply and demand under Board FX-market rules (Art. 211), reinforced by the 6 March 2024 Special MPC market-forces decision and current 2026 monetary reporting; (ii) a broad Art. 212 right to retain FX and transfer inward/outward through licensed channels under Board procedures; (iii) a domestic EGP settlement default; (iv) asymmetric Art. 213 physical-cash border rules; and (v) Arts 214–215 licensed multi-channel FX market supervision. Passage Check ontology posture is left unpublished for Pinpoint/Publication; on existing taxonomy the evaluated candidate leans floating_regulated_market rather than capital_account_regulated, but is not locked in this Evidence Rebuild.
rules.banking_conversion_practicality: Foreign-exchange conversion for the public is available through CBE-supervised banks and through exchange companies and other entities licensed to deal in foreign exchange under Law 194/2020 (Arts 212, 214–215; CBE On-Site Supervision page). FX conversion is therefore a licensed multi-channel activity, not bank-only and not an unregulated free-for-all. Availability of a particular currency, rate or product remains subject to licence scope, Board rules, documentary requirements and commercial terms.

disclaimer: This page provides general informational reference only. Foreign-exchange, monetary-policy and cross-border cash rules in Egypt are subject to change, and transaction-specific requirements may depend on residency or entity status, documentation, amount, licensing and the applicable Central Bank of Egypt / Customs / AML framework. This is not legal, regulatory, tax, financial, or compliance advice. Always verify current rules directly with the Central Bank of Egypt, Egyptian Customs and a licensed intermediary before making any financial or travel decisions.
